text:
Remember me when I have gone

far away into the Silent Land;

when you can no longer hold my hand,

nor I, half turning to go, still wish to stay.

Remember me when every day is ended,

when you no longer tell me of our planned future:

only remember me; you understand

it will be late then for prayers or comfort.

And if you must forget me for a while

and afterward remember, do not grieve:

for if the darkness and the sorrow leave

a trace of all the thoughts I had,

better by far that you forget and smile

than that you remember and be sad.




"Remember"

translation.title: Remember
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's turn from a plea for memory toward a kinder freedom to forget.
